FR-001.title: For an item that asks for dunnage, the step is the dunnage catalogue rendered as a page of the wizard rather than a dialog.

FR-002.title: The catalogue page draws its parts, its pictures and its search from the same source the substitute picker uses; it introduces no second dunnage list.

FR-003.title: The page offers the substitute picker's finding means: one filter matching part number, type or location, and the same picture-visibility choice.

FR-004.title: A chosen part becomes the request's dunnage and is shown as chosen when the page is revisited.

FR-005.title: A generic dunnage request carries exactly one dunnage part, and the flow says a second part is a second request.

FR-006.title: Leaving the page without choosing records no dunnage part and does not advance past a step that requires one.

FR-007.title: A catalogue that cannot be read is reported unavailable with the time of the attempt and a retry, never replaced with a shortened or fabricated list.

FR-008.title: The chosen part appears on the confirmation step, the card and the detail page, with its picture where one exists.

FR-009.title: A part that has left the catalogue since it was chosen is kept on the request and marked as no longer offered, never dropped or replaced.

FR-010.title: Loading is distinguishable from a finished read: progress is shown while loading and a still-loading catalogue is never drawn as empty.

FR-011.title: This chunk deletes the Temp preview source, leaves the build green, and does not rename such an artefact into a permanent-looking name.

FR-012.title: A catalogue that reads successfully and holds no parts is reported as having nothing to offer, never as unavailable.

decisions.decision: Catalogue view model and part row live in MTM_Waitlist.Shared; the control and the step page live in the app project
decisions.why: Shared is the only assembly the Setup and generic-request libraries both reference and it already owns every dunnage picture helper; the app is where reusable controls and page routes already live
decisions.rejected: Putting the whole catalogue in MTM_Waitlist.Setup and adding it as a reference of MTM_Waitlist.GenericRequest

decisions.decision: IDunnageCatalogueReader in Shared, implemented in Setup over IDunnageWorkflowService
decisions.why: The generic flow gets the catalogue shape through a seam and the read keeps the one implementation the substitute dialog already uses
decisions.rejected: Reading sp_Dunnage_Parts_GetAll directly from Shared, which would put a second implementation of the same read in the tree

decisions.decision: A new DunnageCataloguePart row crosses the boundary and SetupDunnagePart is projected to it
decisions.why: SetupDunnagePart has about seventy references across four app pages, the Setup library and tests, several in x:DataType
decisions.rejected: Moving SetupDunnagePart into Shared, which cannot follow a using alias in XAML

decisions.decision: The dunnage step stops using IGenericRequestStepData.ReadDunnageAsync and hosts the shared catalogue view model
decisions.why: The seam is one question and one answer with rows shaped for one list; the catalogue is a stateful shared surface with a filter, a saved preference and a selection
decisions.rejected: Adding a catalogue read to the seam, which would mean two loaders and duplicated attempt-time handling

decisions.decision: The raised request records dunnage.part, dunnage.type, dunnage.picture and dunnage.offered into the existing answers_json, and InputValue carries the chosen part
decisions.why: A generic request has no job snapshot, so the card's picture rule answers nothing and its second line would name nothing
decisions.rejected: Adding a dunnage column to the request table, or reading the catalogue on the board per card

decisions.decision: The shared step frame gains the loading state
decisions.why: Its body is collapsed unless the step is populated, so a hand-rolled ProgressRing inside the body would be hidden during exactly the first load it covers
decisions.rejected: A ProgressRing inside the catalogue control or inside the page body

decisions.decision: The shared catalogue view model returns the load outcome and does not choose surface wording
decisions.why: The dialog keeps its flat failure sentence while the page shows the attempt time and a retry, and A1 forbids changing the dialog
decisions.rejected: Letting the dialog inherit the page's unavailable presentation

decisions.decision: No stored procedure and no schema artifact is added
decisions.why: The read is sp_Dunnage_Parts_GetAll on mtm_receiving_application through the existing service, and the write is the queue's existing submit path
decisions.rejected: A filtered read procedure, which would be a second read path rather than the one source FR-002 requires

decisions.decision: The shared catalogue view model reports a three-outcome result and keeps the substitute dialog's empty-state wording
decisions.why: the dialog's sentences are pinned byte-identical, and the page takes its own words from the new resource keys
decisions.rejected: one wording for both surfaces, which would have changed what the dialog says

decisions.decision: The step frame gained two optional text properties for a step's own loading and unavailable sentences
decisions.why: the pinned wording names a loading line and a sentence carrying the attempt time, and the frame had no place for either
decisions.rejected: drawing the sentences in the page body, which is collapsed in exactly those two states

decisions.decision: A failed catalogue read at raise time records the part as still offered
decisions.why: a read that failed proves nothing, and marking a part gone on the strength of an outage would be a false claim (FR-009)
decisions.rejected: treating any read that does not hold the part as gone, which would mislabel every request raised during an outage

decisions.decision: The dialog view model projects the shared row back onto the Setup part
decisions.why: the Setup workflow adds the part by identifier and its add path reads neither Metadata nor IsSelectedForPair
decisions.rejected: changing ISetupDialogService to hand back the shared row, which would pull the Setup workflow into this chunk

plan.summary: Plan lifts the dunnage catalogue out of the Setup dialog into a shared view model plus a shared control, makes the generic dunnage step a page of that catalogue, gates the step on a chosen part, and carries the part and its picture onto the raised request through answers_json.
plan.key_finding: The catalogue markup cannot be shared from the Setup assembly because MTM_Waitlist.GenericRequest does not reference it, and ClickToEnlargeImageView cannot leave the app because its code-behind calls App.GetService, so the reusable view had to land in the app while only its state went to Shared.

tasks.summary: 32 tasks in 6 phases: Setup 1, Foundational 16 across 7 waves, US1 7 across 5 waves, US2 2, US3 2, Polish 4; 24 tasks marked parallel.

implement.summary: The dunnage step is the plant's catalogue as a page, drawn by one shared control from one read; a chosen part is gated, written to the draft and carried onto the raised request with its picture.

approach: The dunnage catalogue is extracted from the Setup image-search dialog into one shared view model in MTM_Waitlist.Shared and one control in the app, read once through IDunnageCatalogueReader which Setup implements over the existing IDunnageWorkflowService. The generic dunnage step becomes a page that hosts that control, gates its forward button on a chosen part, and writes the chosen part, its type and its picture onto the raised request's answers_json so the confirmation, the card and the detail can name it and draw it.

concerns.note: plan-blocks.py cannot render the calls, code or states blocks on this machine: its template folder .specify/extensions/companion/parts is absent, so part_text() raises FileNotFoundError for call-paths.md, code-pins.md and states.md (only screens.md printed). The plan's Calls, Code pins and States and screens sections were therefore written by hand in the shape screens.md showed. Reinstalling the extension's parts folder would let future plans render them.
